_note: Every dependency below carries an evidence_url pointing at a document that explicitly names its source. The LGFF Capital Funding Allocation Formula fact sheet is unusually good evidence: it lists its input data sources by name, with links.

reports.title: Local Government Fiscal Framework — Capital Funding Allocations
reports.description: Annual allocation of provincial capital funding to Alberta local governments, calculated by a formula set out in the Local Government Fiscal Framework Act. $800 million in 2026.
reports.cadence_note: Aggregate amounts must be communicated by September 30 two years in advance; individual allocations follow some weeks later.

reports.title: Local Government Fiscal Framework — Operating Funding
reports.description: Annual operating funding component of the Local Government Fiscal Framework, $60 million per year, distributed to Alberta local governments.

reports.title: Municipal Affairs Population List (MAPL)
reports.description: Annual official population counts for Alberta municipalities, Metis Settlements and First Nations communities, drawn from municipal or federal census results. Used by provincial ministries to determine municipal grants.
reports.cadence_note: Discontinued in 2020 with the repeal of the Determination of Population Regulation; resumed in 2023 under the Municipal Census Regulation.

reports.title: Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates
reports.publisher: Alberta Treasury Board and Finance, Office of Statistics and Information
reports.description: Annual population estimates for Alberta census subdivisions by year, age and gender, including permanent and non-permanent residents.

reports.title: Municipal Financial Information Return (FIR)
reports.description: Standardised annual return summarising each municipality's audited financial statements — assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses, long term debt and property taxes. Required from every Alberta municipality by May 1.
reports.cadence_note: Due May 1 for the preceding financial year.

reports.title: Municipal Financial and Statistical Data
reports.description: Annual compilation of every Alberta municipality's financial and statistical returns, including tangible capital assets, accumulated amortization, road length, assessment and tax rates.

reports.title: Provincial Equalized Assessment Report
reports.description: Annual adjustment of every municipality's taxable assessment to a common basis, producing a uniform provincial measure of property wealth. Determines each municipality's share of requisitions.

reports.title: Education Property Tax Requisition Comparison Report
reports.description: Annual statement of the education property tax requisition levied on each Alberta municipality, split between residential/farm and non-residential. Municipalities are obliged to collect it on the province's behalf. $3.1 billion in 2025.

dependencies.basis: Calgary and Edmonton allocations weight population at 48 per cent, and the fact sheet names Municipal (Census Subdivision) Population Estimates as the data source.
Calgary and Edmonton allocations weight education property tax requisitions at 48 per cent, sourced from the Education Property Tax Requisition Comparison Report.
Allocations to local governments other than Calgary and Edmonton weight population at 65 per cent, taken from the Municipal Affairs Population List.

Tangible capital assets (15 per cent), five-year average cumulative amortization (10 per cent) and length of local roads (10 per cent) are all drawn from named schedules of the Municipal Financial and Statistical Data.
Needs-based funding eligibility is set by comparing a municipality's equalized assessment per capita, or per kilometre of road, against the provincial average.
The dataset is compiled from the financial information return and statistical information return submitted annually by every Alberta municipality.
Equalized assessment is the means by which the province determines each municipality's contribution to the provincial education property tax requisition.
